'''''Potentilla reptans''''', known as the '''creeping cinquefoil''',<ref>{{PLANTS|id=PORE^|taxon=Potentilla reptans|access-date=13 October 2015}}</ref>  '''European cinquefoil''' or '''creeping tormentil''', is a [[flowering plant]] in the family [[Rosaceae]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-02-02 |title=Potentilla reptans L. Creeping Cinquefoil |url=https://species.nbnatlas.org/species/NBNSYS0000003354 |access-date=2025-02-02 |website=[[National Biodiversity Network]] (NBN Atlas)}}</ref>

== Description ==
A creeping [[perennial plant]] which can reach heights of up to {{Convert abbreviated|20|cm}}.<ref name=":0">{{Cite book |last=Sterry |first=Paul |title=Collins complete guide to British Wildflowers |publisher=HarperCollins Publishers LTD |year=2006 |isbn=9780007236848}}</ref> Its trailing stems can root at the [[Node (botany)|node]]s,<ref name=":0" /> which allows the species to reproduce via vegetative reproduction.<ref>Anten, Niels & Stuefer, Josef & During, Heinjo & Vermeulen, Peter. (2012). Oecologia2013. DOI: 10.1007/s00442-012-2504-8</ref> The [[palmate]] leaves are hairless, attached to long stalks and are divided into 5 to 7 leaflets, with small green leaf-like [[stipule]]s at the base.<ref name=":0" /> The plant blooms between June and September in Europe with flowers that are about 7 mm to 11 mm in diameter with heart-shaped yellow petals. Long stalks support these solitary yellow flowers consisting of 5 petals and sepals with a large number of stamens and carpels at the centre. There are also 5 [[epicalyx]] segments, giving the appearance of 10 sepals.<ref name=":0" />

== Distribution ==

=== Native Range ===
''Potentilla reptans'' has a large [[Native species|native]] distribution across the continents of Europe, Asia, and Africa. In Europe it is native throughout the continent, except Norway where it is introduced.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |date=2025-02-02 |title=''Potentilla reptans'' L. |url=https://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:324739-2 |access-date=2025-02-02 |website=[[Plants of the World Online]] [[Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew]]}}</ref> In Asia it can be found in: Afghanistan, China, Cyprus, Mongolia, Iran, Iraq, Kazakhstan, Kirgizstan, Lebanon, Syria, Pakistan, Israel, Palestine, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan and Uzbekistan.<ref name=":1" /> In Africa it can be found in the countries of: Algeria, Eritrea, Ethiopia, Libya, Morocco and Tunisia.<ref name=":1" />

=== Introduced Range ===
''P. reptans'' has been [[Introduced species|introduced]] outside its native range into various countries across the globe.<ref>{{GRIN|access-date=10 January 2018}}</ref> The species has been widely distributed across North America, where it can be found in the states and territories of: Bermuda, California, Colorado, Florida, Georgia, Illinois, Kentucky, Louisiana, Maryland, Massachusetts, Michigan, Minnesota, New Jersey, New York, Ohio, Oregon, Pennsylvania, Virginia, Washington and Wisconsin.<ref name=":1" /> It has also been introduced in Canada in the provinces of Ontario, Québec and Nova Scotia.<ref name=":1" /> In Oceania the species was also introduced into the countries of Australia and New Zealand.<ref name=":1" />

== Habitat and ecology ==
''P. reptans'' grows in neutral soils, where it utilizes both natural and manmade habitats such as [[Grassland|grasslands]], [[Hedge|hedgerows]], roadsides and [[arable land]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-02-02 |title=Creeping Cinquefoil Potentilla reptans L. |url=https://plantatlas2020.org/atlas/2cd4p9h.94k |access-date=2025-02-02 |website=[[Botanical Society of Britain and Ireland]] Plant Atlas 2020}}</ref> The species can also grow in grass lawns and flowerbeds as an unwanted [[weed]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Fisher |first=Sue |date=2024-07-10 |title=Complete guide to creeping cinquefoil: Is it a weed? |url=https://www.gardenersworld.com/how-to/solve-problems/creeping-cinquefoil/ |access-date=2025-02-02 |website=Gardeners World BBC}}</ref> The grizzled skipper butterfly (''[[Pyrgus malvae]]'') utilizes ''P. reptans'' as a foodplant for its caterpillars.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-02-02 |title=Butterfly Conservation |url=https://butterfly-conservation.org/butterflies/grizzled-skipper |access-date=2025-02-02}}</ref>

== Medicinal uses ==
Alcoholic extracts from roots of ''P. reptans'' showed a moderate antimicrobial activity against common wound pathogens.<ref>{{cite journal |vauthors=Watkins F, Pendry B, Sanchez-Medina A, Corcoran O |date=November 2012 |title=Antimicrobial assays of three native British plants used in Anglo-Saxon medicine for wound healing formulations in 10th century England |url=http://roar.uel.ac.uk/1715/3/2012_Watkins_etal_Antimicrobial.pdf |journal=J Ethnopharmacol |volume=144 |issue=2 |pages=408–15 |doi=10.1016/j.jep.2012.09.031 |pmid=23026307}}</ref>
